# Tableau Cloud export: LOD sheets

A real `unshackle extract tableau` run against a Tableau Cloud site (REST API 3.24),
used by `tests/test_tableau_live_lod_fixture.py`. The content was
created by the live test (`tests/live/test_tableau_live.py`, `LOD_SHEETS` in
`tests/live/tableau/bootstrap.py`) over the fictional Dunder Mifflin data, and deleted
from the site afterwards.

- `workbooks/*.twb`: workbook "Dunder Mifflin LOD" on the published data source "Dunder
  Mifflin Orders" (`datasources/*.tds`, the same as in `tests/fixtures/tableau_live`):
  12 sheets and a dashboard with FIXED, INCLUDE and EXCLUDE LODs, defined as the
  workbook's own calcs. Nine sheets are those of `tests/fixtures/tableau_lod` with the
  same formulas; three are an aggregate of a calc over a FIXED value, a FIXED nested in a
  FIXED, and an aggregated FIXED value under a `status = COMPLETED` filter.
- `views/*.csv`: Tableau's own results for each view (`GET /views/{id}/data`). The
  dashboard's CSV holds the data of some of its sheets.
- `permissions/`, `groups.json`, `metadata/` (Metadata API), and the REST lists.

The workbook XML was generated by the live test and re-serialized by Tableau on publish:
these are the files Tableau Cloud serves back, not files written in Tableau Desktop.

Changes from the raw export, nothing else: the site's host is replaced by
`example.online.tableau.com`, its content URL by `example`, the owner's email by
`user@example.com`, and every LUID by a fake one (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-...`, the same
fake for the same LUID across files); `workbooks.json`, `views.json` and
`datasources.json` keep only the LOD workbook and its data source; the other workbook's
files and `_manifest.json` are dropped.
